findings.title: website_name bypasses the TL0 untrusted-attribute restriction
findings.body:
For TL0 users viewed by anonymous visitors, `website` is deliberately hidden through `untrusted_attributes`, which checks `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. The new `website_name` attribute was added to the plain `attributes` list but not to `untrusted_attributes`, so it is always serialized. It contains the website host, and in the same-domain cases the full path too.

Before this change the client derived the name from `model.website`, which was absent for these users, so nothing was shown. Now `user.hbs` checks `{{#if model.website_name}}` and renders the name in a span for TL0 users.

As a result, new and untrusted (spam) accounts can again advertise their website to anonymous visitors, which is exactly what the restriction exists to prevent. Fix: add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`, or make its include predicate also check `restrict_user_fields?`.

findings.title: include_website_name lacks `?` suffix so it is never used as an include filter
findings.body:
ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_<attr>?` predicates. This method is named `include_website_name` without the `?`, so the serializer never calls it. `website_name` is therefore always emitted (as `null` when there is no website), and any intended gating does not happen.

This is also why the method gives no protection for untrusted users. It should be renamed `include_website_name?`, and it should also apply the same `restrict_user_fields?` check that `website` uses.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic treats unrelated hosts under shared/public suffixes as same domain
findings.body:
The `elsif` branch treats two hosts as the same site whenever everything after the first label matches and the instance host has more than two labels.

For instances hosted on shared domains this gives wrong results. For example, an instance at `forum.trydiscourse.com` (or `x.herokuapp.com`, `x.github.io`, `forum.co.uk`) will show the full URL path for any user website like `spam.trydiscourse.com/...` or `other.co.uk/...`. Those sites are not the instance's domain, so this contradicts the feature's intent.

The comparison is also case-sensitive: `URI#host` preserves case, so `http://Example.com/user` will not match `example.com`.

findings.title: Tests don't cover website_name for TL0/anonymous or the sibling-subdomain branch
findings.body:
The TL0 'untrusted attributes' list does not include `website_name`, and that profile has no website set, so the spec cannot catch that `website_name` leaks for restricted users.

The new `website_name` specs only exercise the identical-host, different-host and parent-domain cases. Nothing tests the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch, a blank website, or a website without a path. The most complex conditional in the method is effectively untested.
